problem: Long-horizon object navigation (ObjectNav, MultiON) is usually tackled with end-to-end RL or modular pipelines whose analytical path planners and exploration modules are rarely studied in isolation. End-to-end agents generalize poorly to new scenes and need retraining for each task variant.
motivation: Pretrained PointGoal agents are near-perfect at reaching a relative goal, so they could replace analytical path planners and avoid learning navigation from scratch. A controlled study of navigation and exploration choices, using oracle detectors and maps to remove confounds, shows which module design choices actually matter.
key_idea: Build a training-free modular object-navigation agent (detector, semantic map, exploration, planner) that reuses a pretrained DD-PPO PointNav policy as the low-level navigator and uses simple uniform random goal sampling for exploration.
insight: A pretrained PointNav policy beats analytical planners (3ON test Success 81 vs 18-21 for FMM/BFS, and only 76 for the ground-truth-mesh shortest-path follower), and runs faster (12h vs 48h per evaluation). Uniform random exploration with a step fail-safe (alpha_exp=50) beats Frontier, Stubborn and ANS (81 vs 72/72/76), because seeing the goal from a distance is enough and HM3D scenes are small. Failure analysis shows most failures come from undiscovered goals (exploration) or missed 'found' actions (PointNav).
method: Object detection: FasterRCNN fine-tuned on 2k oracle-agent frames, plus k-NN colour classification for cylinders (CYL), direct 8-class detection for natural objects (NAT); zero-shot Detic for ObjectNav; confidence threshold 0.95
Map building: projects semantic detections with depth into a 2D top-down grid (0.2 m cells, Chaplot et al. style), assuming perfect depth and odometry; objects once seen stay on the map

Exploration: samples exploration goals from a local grid (10 m for uniform random, 3 m for Stubborn), with Frontier and ANS as alternatives; resamples if the goal is not reached within alpha_exp=50 steps
Planner: picks the current goal category's label-cluster centroid on the map if it has been seen, otherwise the exploration goal, and passes it as a relative goal

Navigation: pretrained DD-PPO PointNav policy (ResNet50 depth encoder + GPS/compass MLP + LSTM, actor/critic heads), compared with shortest-path follower (GT mesh), BFS and FMM with obstacle dilation and an 'Untrap' routine
Agent variants: OracleReveal (GT map), OracleSem (GT semantic labels plus own depth mapping), PredSem (learned detector)
Dataset: MultiON 2.0 on HM3D (800/30/70 scenes, 8M train episodes, 1050 val/test, CYL and NAT objects, distractors, longer episodes)

setting.backbone: Pretrained DD-PPO PointNav (ResNet50+LSTM) as navigator; FasterRCNN + kNN (MultiON) or frozen Detic (ObjectNav) as detector; no ObjectNav training
setting.training_data: PointNav policy pretrained with DD-PPO on HM3D (Matterport3D for the transfer experiment); FasterRCNN fine-tuned on 2k oracle frames for MultiON; no ObjectNav or MultiON policy training; Detic zero-shot
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 256x256 + noiseless GPS+compass + goal category
setting.action_space: low-level: move forward 25 cm, turn left/right 30°, found/stop
setting.privileged: Noiseless GPS+compass and perfect depth/odometry; OracleSem/OracleReveal variants use GT semantic labels or GT map; the shortest-path follower uses GT navmesh (ablation only)

numbers.extra: noiseless sensors; 2500 step limit; mean of 5 seeds; PointNav pretrained on HM3D

numbers_note: MultiON 2.0 is the paper's own dataset; standard deviations are omitted (they are ±1-2).
results: With a pretrained PointNav navigator and uniform random exploration, OracleSem reaches 81% success on 3ON test, far above FMM/BFS planners (18-21%). On HM3D ObjectNav val, PredSem with Detic reaches 30 SR / 14 SPL without ObjectNav training, beating the modular ModLearn (27 SR with Detic, 29 SR / 17 SPL with Mask-RCNN) on SR and ZSON (25/13). It trails supervised PIRLNav (62/28) and OVRL2 (65/28). It also outperforms the end-to-end MultiON baselines on transfer (38 vs 27 best SR on MP3D 3ON).
limitations: Assumes noiseless sensors, perfect depth and odometry, and a static simulated setup
Performance is limited by the object detector (NAT 29% vs CYL 52% SR) and by PointNav's failure to issue 'found'/'stop' near the goal
Uniform exploration relies on small HM3D scenes and random object placement; it does not use semantic priors and may not scale to larger scenes
